questions.q: Why does the KV cache exist in autoregressive decoding?
options: To store the model's gradients between training steps
Because key and value vectors for already-generated tokens never change, so caching them avoids recomputing attention from scratch for the whole sequence at every new token
To reduce the number of parameters in the model
Because GPUs cannot perform matrix multiplication during decoding
questions.explain: Key and value vectors for previously generated tokens are fixed once computed. Caching them turns an O(t squared) recomputation into an O(t) cache lookup plus the new token's work.

questions.q: Which factors determine the size of the KV cache for a single sequence?
options: Only the total number of model parameters
The number of layers, number of KV heads, head dimension, sequence length, and bytes per element (precision)
Only the batch size used during pretraining
The size of the tokenizer's vocabulary
questions.explain: KV cache size is 2 x num_layers x num_kv_heads x head_dim x seq_len x bytes_per_element -- it scales with architecture dimensions, sequence length, and numeric precision.

questions.q: How do grouped-query attention (GQA) and multi-query attention (MQA) reduce KV cache size?
options: By reducing the sequence length the model can process
By reducing the number of distinct key/value heads that must be cached, since multiple (or all) query heads share the same KV head
By storing the cache in a compressed file format on disk
By eliminating the need for a KV cache entirely
questions.explain: GQA shares one KV head across a group of query heads, and MQA shares a single KV head across all query heads, directly shrinking the num_kv_heads term that drives cache size.

questions.q: Why is KV cache memory often the binding constraint on serving batch size, rather than raw GPU compute?
options: Because GPUs have no compute capacity left after loading model weights

Because every concurrent sequence requires its own KV cache, and that cache grows with sequence length, so total cache memory across in-flight requests competes directly with weights for the same limited GPU memory
Because KV cache memory is stored on CPU, not GPU, and is unlimited
Because batch size is fixed by the tokenizer, independent of memory
questions.explain: GPU memory must hold both fixed model weights and a growing KV cache per in-flight sequence. As concurrency or sequence length rises, cache memory -- not compute throughput -- is typically what limits how many requests can be served at once.

questions.q: What does vLLM's PagedAttention technique address?
options: It speeds up the training loop by paging gradients to disk
It manages KV cache memory in non-contiguous blocks, conceptually similar to OS virtual memory paging, to avoid wasting memory on over-allocated sequence slots
It replaces attention entirely with a convolutional operation
It compresses model weights using 4-bit quantization
questions.explain: PagedAttention manages the KV cache in non-contiguous memory blocks rather than pre-allocating a fixed, often wasteful, contiguous buffer per sequence, improving memory utilization during serving.
